Test of correlated random effects (random against fixed effects)

Source: R/cre.R
cre_test.Rd

Wald test that the coefficients of the group means added by cre are all zero. Under the null hypothesis the random effects are uncorrelated with the time-varying regressors, so the random-effects estimates are consistent; a rejection favors fixed effects (or keeping the means in the model). With robust or cluster-robust standard errors the test is a robust version of the Hausman test (Wooldridge 2019).

Usage

cre_test(object, vcov = NULL)

Arguments

object

a model fitted with cre (countreg_rp(), renb() or repois()).

vcov

optional covariance matrix of the estimates (default: the fit's, vcov(object)).

Value

An object of class "htest".

References

Mundlak, Y. (1978). On the pooling of time series and cross section data. Econometrica, 46(1), 69-85.

Wooldridge, J.M. (2019). Correlated random effects models with unbalanced panels. Journal of Econometrics, 211(1), 137-150.

Examples

# \donttest{
data("washington_roads")
m <- repois(Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + offset(lnlength), group_var = "ID",
            data = washington_roads, cre = ~ lnaadt, stderr = "robust")
cre_test(m)
#> 
#> 	Wald test of correlated random effects (group means)
#> 
#> data:  repois(formula = Total_crashes ~ lnaadt + offset(lnlength), group_var = "ID",      data = washington_roads, stderr = "robust", cre = ~lnaadt)
#> Wald chi-squared = 7.8392, df = 1, p-value = 0.005113
#> sample estimates:
#> mean_lnaadt 
#>    1.861682 
#> 
# }
